scope: Program-level compliance requirements that the platform must satisfy, taken only from the Associates Operating Agreement, the Program Policies, the Standard Commission Income Statement and FTC materials. Each requirement carries a verbatim or near-verbatim quote and a source id.

requirements.requirement: The site must clearly and prominently state the Associate identification statement.
requirements.quote: “You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: ‘As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.’”
requirements.how_implemented: The statement appears in the persistent header disclosure bar and in the footer of every page generated by build.py.

requirements.topic: Link-level disclosure must be clear and conspicuous
requirements.requirement: Beyond the site-wide statement, each affiliate link needs a clear, nearby, FTC-compliant disclosure.
requirements.quote: “To comply with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) regulations, your link-level disclosure must be: 1. Clear. A clear disclosure could be as simple as ‘(paid link)’, ‘#ad’, or ‘#CommissionsEarned’. 2. Conspicuous. It should be placed near any affiliate link or product review in a location that customers will notice easily. They shouldn't have to hunt for it.”
requirements.how_implemented: Every outbound Amazon button carries a visible “Paid link” tag, and a disclosure note sits directly beneath each CTA.

requirements.requirement: Disclosures must be hard to miss, in the same medium as the endorsement, and must not be buried or mixed into hashtags.
requirements.quote: “Make sure people will see and understand the disclosure. Place it so it's hard to miss. The disclosure should be placed with the endorsement message itself. Disclosures are likely to be missed if they appear only on an ABOUT ME or profile page, at the end of posts or videos, or anywhere that requires a person to click MORE. Don't mix your disclosure into a group of hashtags or links.”
requirements.how_implemented: Disclosure bar is above the fold on every page; per-link badges; no disclosure-only-in-footer pattern.

requirements.requirement: A financial relationship with the seller must be disclosed.
requirements.quote: 16 CFR §255.5 requires disclosure of material connections between an endorser and the seller that would materially affect the weight or credibility of the endorsement.
requirements.how_implemented: Commission-earning relationship disclosed in the header, on each CTA and on the compliance page.

requirements.requirement: Prices and availability may only be displayed if Amazon serves them or they are obtained through Creators API/PA API.
requirements.quote: “Because prices for and availability of Products that you have listed on your Site may change, your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements…”
requirements.how_implemented: No Amazon price or availability is shown anywhere. Manufacturer list prices are shown separately and explicitly labelled as brand-site prices with their own source link.

requirements.requirement: Amazon reviews/star ratings may only be displayed when obtained through Creators API or PA API.
requirements.quote: “You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License.”
requirements.how_implemented: Amazon stars/review counts blank and flagged. Brand-hosted ratings are shown only in a clearly separate column, attributed to the brand's own site.

requirements.topic: No price tracking or price alerts
requirements.requirement: Sites must not offer price tracking or price alerting unless Amazon agrees otherwise.
requirements.quote: “Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.”
requirements.how_implemented: The platform blueprint explicitly rules out price-history charts and alerts; ‘pricing analysis’ is limited to brand-published list prices and unit economics computed from them.

requirements.requirement: No bidding on Amazon or Kindle trademarks, or any Amazon Mark, in paid search.
requirements.quote: “…any Product purchased by a customer who is referred to an Amazon Site through any advertisement that you purchased, including through participation in bidding or auctions on keywords, search terms, or other identifiers that include the word ‘amazon’, or ‘kindle’, or any other Amazon Mark…” (disqualified purchases)
requirements.how_implemented: Guardrail G3 in the platform blueprint: a negative-keyword list containing Amazon Marks is enforced in the paid-acquisition workflow.

requirements.topic: No API content aggregation, analysis or model training
requirements.requirement: Creators API / PA API / Data Feeds content may not be aggregated, analysed, repurposed, or used to train or fine-tune ML models.
requirements.quote: “You will not, without our express prior written approval, access or use Creators API, PA API or Data Feeds for the purpose of aggregating, analyzing, extracting, or repurposing any Product Advertising Content or in connection with any software or other application intended for use by persons or entities that offer products on an Amazon Site, or in the direct training or fine-tuning of a machine learning and/or foundational model.”
requirements.how_implemented: Architectural constraint: any AI research/trend scoring runs only on the operator's own first-party data (clicks, conversions, revenue) and public manufacturer data. Program Content is display-only, never a training or analytics input.

requirements.requirement: Sites must carry robust original content — roughly 10+ posts, recent, publicly available.
requirements.quote: “All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) – a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts. They must be publicly available…” and “Content on your website must be recent (generally within the last 60 days). You must own your website.”
requirements.how_implemented: This build ships analysis, comparison and buying-guide pages written for this dataset, plus the platform blueprint — not a thin link list.

requirements.requirement: Applications are reviewed after three qualifying sales within the first 180 days; personal orders do not count.
requirements.quote: “After you sign up, our Associates team will check your application once you’ve driven qualified sales (we require at least three within the first 180 days). Please note that personal orders do not qualify.”
requirements.how_implemented: Launch sequencing in the blueprint: publish the buying guide + three product pages first, then apply, so the 180-day clock starts with live traffic.

requirements.topic: No incentive for using links; no self-purchase
requirements.requirement: No rewards/loyalty schemes driving clicks; no buying through your own links or asking friends/family to.
requirements.quote: “You will not offer any person or entity any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links…” / “You will not directly or indirectly purchase any Product(s)… through Special Links…”
requirements.how_implemented: No incentives, no contests, no employee purchase flows. Guardrail G4.

requirements.topic: No framing, no cloaking, no redirecting links
requirements.requirement: Amazon pages may not be framed; Special Links may not be cloaked; redirecting links that skip user action are prohibited.
requirements.quote: “You will not frame an Amazon Site, or any part of it, within your Site…” / “You will not cloak, hide, spoof, or otherwise obscure the URL of your Site containing Special Links (including by use of Redirecting Links)…”
requirements.how_implemented: No iframes. Outbound links point straight at the Amazon URL; no interstitial or meta-refresh forwarding is generated by the site.

requirements.requirement: Reporting IDs are permitted, but they may not be tied to an individual end user.
requirements.quote: “…we may issue you additional ‘sub-tag’ Associate IDs that permit you to monitor and optimize the performance of your Special Links… Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users’ behavior).”
requirements.how_implemented: Sub-tags are assigned per channel/page, never per visitor. Documented as guardrail G5.

requirements.requirement: Amazon Marks may be used only to advertise availability of products on an Amazon Site, alongside a corresponding Special Link, unaltered, and never in offline material.
requirements.quote: “YOU ARE ALLOWED TO USE THE AMAZON MARKS ONLY BY DISPLAY ON YOUR SITE WITH THE PURPOSE OF ADVERTISING AVAILABILITY OF PRODUCTS ON AN AMAZON SITE, WITH A CORRESPONDING SPECIAL LINK TO THAT SITE.”
requirements.how_implemented: No Amazon logo is used in this build; Amazon is referred to in plain text next to real Special Links only.

requirements.requirement: No inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or misleading product/policy/price claims; no claiming an experience you have not had.
requirements.quote: “You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices.” / FTC: “You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried.”
requirements.how_implemented: No hands-on testing claims are made anywhere. Copy is explicitly framed as documentation-based analysis, and every factual line links to the manufacturer page or manual.

attribution_windows.value: 24 hours, or earlier if the customer orders a non-digital product or clicks another Special Link
Order must be completed no later than 89 days after the initial click-through
Approximately 60 days following the end of the calendar month in which commission was earned
